children: The Singapore dollar weakens against the greenback in the Asian session, as the escalating conflict in the Middle East squeezes global oil supplies. The market is still focusing on Middle East developments, says Quek Ser Leang of UOB Global Economics & Markets Research in a note. Any escalation in geopolitical tensions is likely to fuel concerns over global energy supplies and add to inflation risks, the senior technical strategist adds. The U.S. dollar rises 0.1% to 1.2684 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
